positive: Many commenters praise the opening and closing animation as smooth, clean and clever, including some who say they usually prefer other brands.
Several note the inner screen appears to have almost no visible crease, crediting the matte finish for helping hide it.
A few see the angle-responsive animation as a sign apps can detect hinge position, and treat it as a design highlight.
negative: Several commenters downplay the fold animation as a gimmick, noting that a rival phone's owner reportedly recreated it quickly, so it doesn't justify the price.
Some worry about high prices and expensive repairs, saying the cost is excessive compared with competing foldables.

positive: Several self-described Samsung foldable users say they are surprised and impressed by how polished Apple's first foldable looks, especially its software animation.
Some commenters stay loyal to Samsung, credit it for the display and for pushing foldables, and say Samsung remains innovative.
Others expect the launch to build big hype and push competitors to respond, changing the foldable market, with praise for build quality and MagSafe.
negative: Many commenters say foldables and features like split screen have existed on Samsung and Android phones for years, so Apple's version is seen as very late.
Commenters mock Apple fans for getting excited about familiar features, and say Apple is copying Samsung or presenting old technology as new.
Some point out Apple once dismissed foldables, and others note Samsung supplies Apple's screens. A few predict Apple will drop the product quickly.

positive: Many viewers were pleasantly surprised by the Duo's design, praising its minimal crease, matte inner screen, unfolding animation and software polish despite initial skepticism.
Some commenters think the Samsung Fold 8 looks better, citing its thin, light, symmetrical, rectangular design, and several say they already own one.
Others argue the Duo's advantages are its more usable aspect ratio, ecosystem, and expected durability, with some saying they will buy it despite tradeoffs.
negative: Many commenters say Apple is entering foldables years after Samsung and Google, yet presents the idea as new, and they criticise fans who echo that framing.
The price is seen as too high, with some saying it costs as much as an iPhone plus an iPad, or more than Samsung's equivalent.
The outer screen's shape, aspect ratio and rounded corners are called odd or impractical, and several say Samsung's front screen and software features, like desktop mode, are better.

positive: Many commenters expected a higher launch price, often well above the actual figure, and are pleasantly surprised it wasn't more expensive.
The price is seen as competitive with Samsung's foldables and in line with what foldables typically cost, even after accounting for inflation.
Some welcome the pricing as a sign of growing foldable competition, which they think should push all makers to improve.
negative: Many commenters say the foldable is far too expensive and out of reach for most people, with the price becoming a joke about the 'Duo' name.
Viewers in India and Mexico say local prices are especially steep compared with local incomes and with rival foldables or other purchases.
Some say rising electronics prices have become unreasonable and that a large investment is hard to justify for a device they want to use less.

positive: Many commenters prefer an uninterrupted inner screen over a visible cutout or dot, and they see the hidden camera as a sensible trade-off.
Several say they rarely take selfies on the inner display and would use the outer screen camera, so lower image quality matters little to them.
Some praise the polished camera animation and transition when folding and unfolding, and expect rivals to improve under-display camera tech in response.
negative: Commenters think the hidden camera lowers image quality, which is why it fell out of favor. Many prefer a visible punch-hole for better selfies.

positive: Many left-handed commenters say they are used to right-handed designs and have adapted, so the dock placement is not a deal breaker.
Some suggest software fixes such as a left-side dock or a lefty mode, or rotating the device, and defend the layout as a sensible design choice.
negative: Many left-handed commenters say the Duo's layout and interface favor right-handed one-handed use, making it awkward or frustrating for them.
Hardware features like the fingerprint sensor, outer display, and cameras sit on one side, so software tweaks alone may not fix usability for lefties.

positive: Apple Pencil compatibility is a surprise highlight that pushed several viewers, including some Android foldable owners, toward buying or pre-ordering the device.
Pencil support is seen as an advantage over Samsung's foldable, which lacks pen input; some hope Samsung brings its stylus back.
Pencil support is valued alongside the larger inner screen, which makes the device feel like a mini iPad for productivity and note-taking.
negative: Many commenters say Apple is copying or following Samsung and other makers, and that fans overpraise it as an innovator.
Some see Apple Pencil support on a foldable as a blow to Samsung, and want S Pen support restored on its foldables.
Others worry a hard pencil tip could scratch or damage the inner folding screen, and complain about the high price and lack of base Pencil support.

positive: Many commenters praise the smooth open and close transition animation, saying it makes the outer screen feel like transparent glass revealing the inner display.
The nano-texture inner display is welcomed for its matte look, reduced glare, less visible fold crease and fewer fingerprints.
Some see it pairing well with Apple Pencil support, comparing the feel to paper-style screen protectors, and count it among the phone's strengths.
negative: The change from the glossy outer display to the matte inner one looks odd, and some say the crease was already barely noticeable.
Commenters worry about the inner screen's durability, since it can't take a screen protector, and about scratches when the phone is left open.

positive: Many commenters are eager to pre-order or try the Duo as soon as it launches, with several counting down to the order date.
Owners of older iPhones, such as Pro Max models, say the Duo is the upgrade they have been waiting for.
Some are drawn by the new foldable design and by the chance to replace both an iPhone and a tablet. Others expect strong sales despite the price.
negative: Many find the price far too high, especially outside the US, and say it is hard to justify over a Pro Max or an iPad mini.
Many plan to wait for a later generation, expecting better refinement, lower prices, and fewer first-version problems, including screen durability concerns.
Some are put off by the weight, the camera and feature compromises, and the similarity to a small tablet, so they prefer a Pro Max.

positive: Several commenters like Apple's folio case: it looks good, protects better than foldable cases they've seen, and keeps the front screen free of smudges and scratches.
The case's built-in stand option is seen as practical for propping the phone up sideways.
Many viewers are drawn to the Duo's design and features, including smooth fold animations and MagSafe, though some say the price holds them back.
negative: Folio and kickstand cases are seen as awkward: the cover blocks the camera, quick payments and any outside view, and it leaves edges exposed.
Commenters worry the phone is already heavy, thick and bulky, and a case makes it larger and heavier still.
Some question how to protect the outer screen from scratches, and whether a case would reduce wobble when the phone is open.

positive: Many commenters expect a well-known durability YouTuber to put the phone through bend and stress tests, and some joke that it will break.
Some think Apple designed it with such tests in mind, pointing to reinforced areas such as the antenna lines, and expect it to hold up.
Viewers are excited about the design, though some are cautious about a first-generation device and would wait for durability to be proven.
negative: Commenters worry the foldable screen scratches easily, with some noting deeper marks appearing at moderate scratch-test levels.
Many expect the fold crease to become visible within a few months of regular use.
Several doubt the phone's overall toughness, citing drop fragility, antenna line placement and the high price given unproven durability, and want teardown and bend tests.

positive: Many commenters are choosing between a dark blue-black shade and white, with the darker option slightly more often named as the favorite.
Some prefer white for its jewelry-like look or because the dark finish makes the bezels look larger. Others find the dark blue-black attractive and understated.
Several plan to buy at launch, often with higher storage tiers, and some want to pair the phone with a taupe folio case.
negative: Many commenters worry about battery life, doubting the quoted figures and wanting clearer information on battery size and charge level display.
Storage tiers are seen as very expensive in Australia and New Zealand, with local prices well above currency-converted US pricing.
Some dislike the color options and names, wanting a plain black, and feel the inner display's color accuracy is lacking.

positive: Many commenters like the compact folded shape, saying it brings back small phones like the mini while still opening to a big screen for media.
Several praise the software and design details, such as the smooth open/close animation, screen transitions, and side toolbar, and say a foldable is hard to give up.
negative: Many commenters say the foldable design is not new, pointing to earlier devices like the Surface Duo and existing Android foldables, so Apple is seen as late or copying.
Some say the folded device looks too big or awkward for pockets and one-handed use, with a few saying a tablet would make more sense.
Several raise design concerns: a covered front screen, no Face ID, a worse camera or selfie setup, and screens that may be fragile.

positive: Many commenters say Apple's tight hardware and software integration is its main strength, describing the Duo's software as polished, smooth and carefully designed.
Several say the software, including the animations and new ways of interacting, makes them interested in a foldable or in switching from Android.
Some note rivals offer more features and flexibility, but Apple's refinement, ecosystem and expected app support are seen as the reasons it will sell.
negative: Many commenters say Apple's foldable and its software features are not new, pointing to Samsung and Microsoft devices and mocking the idea that Apple pioneered them.
Several say the software is the only real selling point, doubt it justifies the long wait, and expect slow app support from developers.
Some argue software quality can undermine good hardware, citing a rival foldable's OS, while others dispute Apple's advantage over Samsung or Android.

positive: Many commenters are excited about the iPhone Duo, saying they plan to buy or pre-order it, and some Android users express admiration.
The fold transition animation and software polish get repeated praise, with some saying Android makers should focus more on UI and animation.
Weight and thickness against Samsung's foldable come up often, with some defending the heft as a result of premium materials.
negative: Many commenters mock the name and the lack of imagination behind it, saying a different name such as a fold-themed one would have fit better.
The name and design draw comparisons to the Microsoft Surface Duo and to Samsung, with the phone seen as borrowing from both.
Jokes about the Duo name focus on its weight, high price and expected small yearly upgrades, with some saying the shape bothers their need for symmetry.

positive: Commenters defend the phone against durability worries, noting that the folding demo unit was a plastic dummy while the real device uses titanium.
Many say the price is justified by the two screens and was never meant to signal pro-level features, and that other foldables cost similar amounts.
Fans are excited by the fold animation and Apple's software and ecosystem, and several say this is the first foldable they want to buy.
negative: Many expect the fold crease to wear out the phone over months of regular use.
Commenters fear one drop could destroy it, and doubt that cases can protect a folding device well.
At roughly $2,000, a fragile and heavy design seems hard to justify, especially when rival foldables already exist.

positive: Many viewers praise the design and polish, especially the smooth opening animation, the camera bump orientation, and how the software suits the foldable's look.
Several commenters see practical value in the larger screen and portrait use, such as reading documents or patient charts on the go.
Others say they're excited for the foldable market, with some comparing it to Samsung foldables and crediting the screen or the Apple ecosystem.
negative: Many commenters like the Duo's look but say the price, around 2,000 dollars or more, is too high. Some would wait for a sale or skip a first-generation product.
Several raise practical drawbacks: a visible crease, rounded corners that reduce usable screen, camera compromises, no Face ID, a matte finish that hurts contrast, and a large size.
Some commenters respond sarcastically, questioning how a phone no one has used yet can be called great. Others dispute claims of Apple innovation, noting foldables and similar features already exist.

positive: Many commenters see the foldable as a way to carry one pocketable device instead of both an iPhone and an iPad or iPad mini.
A larger inner screen is valued for video, gaming, multitasking, reading, and viewing plans or manuals for work, with some citing easier reading for aging eyes.
Design details draw praise, including the screen animation, matte finish, button placement, and wide passport-style shape. A few compare it favorably with other foldables.
negative: Many see the Duo as essentially a small iPad in a folding body, and as late to a category rivals already cover, with little real innovation.
The matte inner screen draws criticism for looking dull and washed out in sunlight, and repair and replacement costs are seen as excessive compared with rivals.

Software feels limited: crowded home screen, few dock apps, awkward multitasking gestures, no landscape split-screen, and doubts developers will use the extra space. Some would rather see core reliability fixed.

positive: Many commenters say iOS adapted for the foldable looks polished and well integrated, and that software is what makes the device appealing.
Several people who had no interest in foldables, including some Android users, say Apple's version has changed their mind or impressed them.
negative: Many commenters say the price is too high, and that it becomes far worse in countries like India and Brazil once taxes and conversion apply.
Several say Android foldables already offer the same features, that iOS multitasking is less mature, and that Android users have little reason to switch.
Others criticise the design: a visible crease, a poor opening mechanism, and reviewers who dodge the issues or downplay the cost.

positive: Commenters praise the hinge as properly engineered, contrasting it with hollow mockups and calling it more thoughtful than copies of other foldables.
Many doubt the device would break easily, citing sturdy hardware and a durable laptop hinge as evidence that well-built hinges last.
Several like the rounded, booklet-like edges and the one-sided asymmetry, saying they feel softer, are easier to hold and look good closed.
negative: Commenters doubt that an IP68 rating means much on a foldable, since the hinge area is open to dust and the protection may wear off over time.
Some worry the hinge will wear out or fail with frequent opening and closing, and say they would not take a pricey foldable to the beach unprotected.
Others note that rival foldables with similar ratings still let dust into the hinge or failed, so they expect the same here.

positive: Many commenters are excited about the foldable iPhone and plan to buy it at launch or preorder, often depending on trade-in deals.
Some prefer to wait for a later generation or compare other foldables and camera phones before deciding, while trusting Apple's durability testing.
Viewers like the polished design, attention to detail and camera use with the folded display, and expect early issues to be fixed by updates.
negative: Many commenters say Apple is late to foldable phones, which other brands have offered for years, and that the device is not innovative.
Several expect Apple to hold back features such as a flagship or telephoto camera and add them in later models, calling it a marketing pattern.
Others object to the high price, the basic cameras, the large bezel and the closed shape, and say these make them want to wait for a better version.

positive: Several commenters like the Duo's design but wish it had Pro-level cameras, though others say it isn't a Pro model, so nothing is sacrificed.
Many are interested but cautious, planning to wait for later versions or keep their current Pro phones, partly because of the high price.
Commenters praise the build, citing a thin titanium frame, durability like the iPhone Air, and weight that compares well with a cased phone.
negative: Many commenters say the Duo's cameras fall short of the Pro's, such as the missing telephoto and main lens, and would buy it if they matched.
The price is a major objection, especially in countries like India, Canada and Australia where local costs are far higher; some fear weak sales.
Other missing features also deter buyers, including no Face ID, a matte display, weaker battery, extra weight, speakers, and the look of the device.

positive: Fingerprint unlock is described as fast and practical, for example at a desk or when entering a PIN often, and some call Face ID gimmicky or distracting.
Watch unlock support and Pencil compatibility are cited as features that won over people who were unsure about the device.
negative: Missing Face ID is a dealbreaker for many commenters, who say it alone makes them skip the device.
Some find a fingerprint sensor inconvenient or impractical, for example with arthritic hands, and worry about smudges on the device.

text.text: EXAMPLE · iPhone Duo on YouTube: weekly readout

*Lift concentrates in small channels; audience sentiment is split, with Samsung and price debates leading comments.*
212 videos from 160 creators drew 227.3M views. 25.4% of videos outperformed and 27.7% underperformed their own channel norms. Across 7,014 scored comments (166 videos), sentiment is 39.3% positive and 34.0% negative. Small channels outperform most often; large channels rarely do and read net negative. Comment intent leans toward buying (802) over skipping (593), with 361 waiting for an upgrade. Since the last refresh, positive share slipped 1.2 points.

elements.text: Example of the Slack digest, to show the format. Figures are illustrative and not guaranteed to be accurate. Ask a follow-up: mention the app or message it. The full report is in your inbox.

examples.q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
examples.a:
Small channels break out most: 36% of their videos outperformed their baseline (n=89 videos), versus 22% for mid-size channels (n=50) and 5.3% for large channels (n=38). Average relative lift follows the same order: about 8.0x for small, 3.7x for mid, 1.3x for large.

Audiences are mostly lukewarm. Net sentiment on product-side comments is slightly positive for small channels (+0.061, n=2,714 comments) and a bit better for mid (+0.109, n=2,335). Large channels are slightly negative (-0.025, n=1,965), with more negative (38.8%) than positive (36.2%) comments.

So mid-size channels pair decent breakout rates with the happiest audiences, while large channels do worst on both measures. Caveat: these are associations from a comment sample, not causes, and the large group has the fewest videos.
examples.sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier LIKE 'nano%' OR cr.tier LIKE 'micro%' THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier LIKE 'mid%' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier LIKE 'macro%' OR cr.tier LIKE 'mega%' THEN 'large' END AS size_group, p.outperformer, p.rel_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'), vid AS (SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift FROM base WHERE outperformer IS NOT NULL GROUP BY size_group), com AS (SELECT b.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='positive' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='negative' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='positive' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)-AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='negative' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN base b ON b.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY b.size_group) SELECT v.size_group, v.n_videos_with_baseline, v.outperformer_rate, v.avg_rel_lift, c.n_product_side, c.pct_positive, c.pct_negative, CASE WHEN c.n_product_side>=10 THEN c.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment FROM vid v LEFT JOIN com c ON c.size_group=v.size_group ORDER BY v.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
examples.a:
First impressions looks like the best-supported format for mid-sized channels. It has the largest sample (n=19 videos), and 42% of those videos outperformed their baseline. Mean relative lift was 2.7, and net sentiment was positive at +0.23 (n=1,028 product-side comments).

Full review and durability test both show a 100% outperformer rate, but each is a single video, so I wouldn't draw conclusions from them.

Explainer/tips (n=8) is mixed. Only 12.5% outperformed, yet mean lift was 9.7, which suggests one or two big hits are skewing the average. Sentiment was slightly negative (-0.06).

Comparison (n=6), upgrade advice (n=8), meme shorts (n=4) and keynote recaps (n=2) had no outperformers.

Caveat: these are associations, not causes, and most formats have small samples.
examples.sql: WITH vids AS (SELECT c.video_id, c.format, p.rel_lift, p.lift, p.outperformer FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M'), perf AS (SELECT format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, SUM(CASE WHEN outperformer IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS mean_rel_lift FROM vids GROUP BY format), sent AS (SELECT v.format, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='positive' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_pos, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='negative' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_neg FROM vids v JOIN comments m ON m.video_id=v.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY v.format) SELECT perf.format, perf.n_videos, perf.n_with_baseline, perf.outperformer_rate, perf.mean_rel_lift, sent.n_product_side, CASE WHEN sent.n_product_side>=10 THEN ROUND(sent.pct_pos - sent.pct_neg,3) END AS net_sentiment FROM perf LEFT JOIN sent ON sent.format=perf.format ORDER BY perf.outperformer_rate DESC, perf.mean_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
examples.a:
Two high-lift videos stand out for the most negative reaction. "iPhone Duo's Camera Disappears #shorts" (Time Travel Visuals) has a lift of 499.28 (rel_lift 72.9) on 20.5M views. Among product-side comments (n=76), about 70% were negative and 11% positive, so net sentiment is -0.59. "iPhone FOLD Hands-On | Apple COOKED!" (TechDroider) has a lift of 86.8 (rel_lift 12.7) on 2.0M views. Among product-side comments (n=56), about 70% were negative and 18% positive, so net sentiment is -0.52.

Lift and sentiment are separate measures here. Both videos spread widely, and the reaction under them is mostly critical.

Caveat: these are sampled comments, with n of 56 to 76 per video, and the result shows associations, not causes.
examples.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, AVG(sentiment='positive') AS pct_pos, AVG(sentiment='negative') AS pct_neg FROM comments WHERE lang='en' AND trivial=0 AND target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY video_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=10) SELECT ct.video_id, ct.title, cr.name AS creator, ct.format, p.views, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, s.n_product_side, ROUND(s.pct_pos,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(s.pct_neg,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(s.pct_pos - s.pct_neg,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content ct JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id = ct.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id = ct.video_id JOIN s ON s.video_id = ct.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, p.rel_lift DESC LIMIT 10

examples.q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
examples.a:
Largest topics by total comments: "Samsung Did It First" (n=820), praise for review quality (n=543), price complaints (n=478), Apple ad parody humor (n=466), and "Eager to Buy" (n=461).

Fastest growing this week versus last, among topics with prior-week n of at least 10:
- Left-handed concerns: 89 vs 13, about +585%
- "Waiting for Next Year": 51 vs 10, +410%
- Wanting pro cameras: 38 vs 11, +246%
- Apple ad parody humor: 113 vs 37, +205%
- Under-display camera: 95 vs 32, +197%

By raw added comments, "Samsung Did It First" gained the most (+128, to 210), followed by "Eager to Buy" (+99).

Caveat: the top percentage gains start from small bases (prior n of 10 to 13), so they can swing a lot. Several other topics had too little prior-week data to show growth.
examples.sql: WITH mx AS (SELECT max(day_since_launch) AS d FROM comments), c AS (SELECT cm.topic_id, cm.day_since_launch AS dsl FROM comments cm JOIN content v ON v.video_id = cm.video_id WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND cm.topic_id IS NOT NULL) SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, count(*) AS n_total, sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl > mx.d-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl <= mx.d-7 AND c.dsl > mx.d-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prev_week, sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl > mx.d-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl <= mx.d-7 AND c.dsl > mx.d-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS abs_change, CASE WHEN sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl <= mx.d-7 AND c.dsl > mx.d-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 10 THEN round(1.0*(sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl > mx.d-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl <= mx.d-7 AND c.dsl > mx.d-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) / sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl <= mx.d-7 AND c.dsl > mx.d-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 3) END AS wow_growth, mx.d AS latest_day FROM c JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = c.topic_id CROSS JOIN mx GROUP BY t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, mx.d ORDER BY n_total DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: What do people like most about the Duo, and what do they criticise most?
examples.a:
Most-liked: Samsung comparisons and buying interest. Most-criticised: price and durability. But the same topics show up on both sides, so these are really the main debates rather than clear likes or dislikes.

Liked (positive comments, out of 6,104 product comments):
- "Samsung Did It First" had 320 positive comments (5.2% of all comments).
- "Eager to Buy" had 212, and 46% of its comments were positive (n=461).
- "Samsung Fold Comparisons" had 200, and 48% were positive (n=417).

Criticised (negative comments):
- "Samsung Did It First" had 324 negative comments.
- Price complaints had 197 (n=478, 41% negative).
- Durability doubts had 179 (n=452, 40%).
- The under-display camera had 124 (n=299, 42%).

Caveat: these are sampled comments, and the sentiment labels are imperfect. Positive and negative counts for most topics are close, so treat the ranking as indicative only.
examples.sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.comment_id, c.sentiment, t.topic_id, t.name FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=c.topic_id WHERE c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND t.pool='product'), agg AS (SELECT topic_id, name, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(sentiment='positive') AS pos, SUM(sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM base GROUP BY topic_id, name), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_n FROM base) SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'liked' AS side, name AS topic, n AS topic_n, pos AS side_n, ROUND(pos*1.0/n,3) AS share_of_topic, ROUND(pos*1.0/total_n,3) AS share_of_all_product_comments, total_n FROM agg, tot ORDER BY pos DESC LIMIT 8) UNION ALL SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'criticised' AS side, name, n, neg, ROUND(neg*1.0/n,3), ROUND(neg*1.0/total_n,3), total_n FROM agg, tot ORDER BY neg DESC LIMIT 8)
